decisions.decision: Commit the REAL nonprod secret values, age-encrypted, rather than placeholders
decisions.rationale: User-chosen after being shown the trade. Only this shape pays off: it deletes the Read(.env.*) deny friction, the seed-worktree-env wrapper, and worktree env seeding entirely, because the encrypted file arrives via git. A placeholder file keeps all three problems. Accepted: ciphertext of real nonprod credentials is in git history permanently, and rotation means re-encrypt + commit.

decisions.decision: The gitleaks allowlist for secrets.enc.env is by-path only, and ships paired with an encryption assertion
decisions.rationale: An allowlisted path with no assertion that the file is genuinely encrypted is exactly how a plaintext secret ships silently later. pnpm secrets:check asserts SOPS ciphertext, runs on the INDEX in pre-commit and on disk in CI, and also fails if the paths literal stops matching its copy in the script. Neither half ships alone.

decisions.decision: ci.yml is the single source of truth for the gitleaks version; the install script and the drift guard parse it
decisions.rationale: CI's scanner was UNPINNED — gitleaks-action installs the latest release at run time, so the enforced rule set changed between runs with nothing in the repo recording which one passed. Pinned to 8.30.1. The version literal appears exactly once so local and CI cannot diverge.

decisions.decision: Local e2e belongs in the default pre-push tier, with an explicit agent-facing callout
decisions.rationale: User's call, made after a stale claim was corrected: local e2e does NOT wipe the shared nonprod backend. Since 5f325f8 resets are targeted per user id from a per-run registry; fullReset() is manual-only; probeResetCapability() refuses to start against a backend still serving the old wiping contract. CI's e2e job is ~1m41s for 57 specs, so the time cost is acceptable.

decisions.decision: The full test suite does NOT go on pre-commit
decisions.rationale: Pre-commit is for the irreversible or the cheap; pre-push is for the expensive and correctness-related. A secret in a commit needs history rewriting, so it belongs on pre-commit. A failing test does not. Decisive here: this repo does TDD with RED commits, where a commit containing a failing test is a supported workflow — a full-suite pre-commit gate makes red-green-refactor impossible without --no-verify and trains bypass reflex.

decisions.decision: pnpm was starting twice; global pnpm realigned to the repo's packageManager pin
decisions.rationale: Global pnpm was 11.22.0 while package.json pins 11.20.0. pnpm 11's switchCliVersion sees the mismatch and re-executes the entire CLI as a synchronous child process, so every invocation in this repo paid two full pnpm boots. npm install -g pnpm@11.20.0 took pnpm --version from ~1991ms to ~669ms (orchestrator re-verified: 0.74-0.81s). None of the suspected causes (nvm prefix conflict, NODE_OPTIONS, shell function, /mnt/c, store size) were responsible.
